categories.main_business_segments: VeriSilicon primarily operates in two main business segments: semiconductor IP licensing and one-stop chip customization services. The IP licensing includes processor IPs such as GPU, NPU, VPU, DSP, ISP, and display processing IPs, as well as analog, mixed-signal, and RF IPs. The chip customization services cover chip design and volume production services, catering to diverse customer needs across various industries.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced semiconductor IP technologies including GPU, NPU, VPU, DSP, ISP, and display processors, with strong capabilities in AI acceleration and low-power designs. It supports multiple process nodes from traditional CMOS to advanced FinFET (14nm to 5nm) and FD-SOI (28nm, 22nm) technologies. VeriSilicon employs a Silicon Platform as a Service (SiPaaS) model, integrating IP cores with chip design and software development, and actively develops Chiplet technology for modular chip architectures and advanced packaging solutions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: VeriSilicon serves a broad range of customers including chip design companies, IDM, system manufacturers, large internet companies, cloud service providers, and automotive OEMs. Key application markets include AI computing (AIGC), data centers, automotive electronics (including ADAS and autonomous driving), wearable devices (smartwatches, AR/VR glasses), IoT, consumer electronics, and industrial sectors. The company has established partnerships with global leaders such as Samsung, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and major Chinese internet firms.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally with subsidiaries and R&D centers in China (Shanghai, Beijing, Chengdu, Nanjing, Hainan), the United States (Silicon Valley, Dallas), Europe (France), Japan, Hong Kong, and Vietnam. Its revenue is derived from both domestic (approximately 62.57%) and international markets (approximately 37.43%), with significant sales growth in overseas markets in 2024.
categories.supply_chain_position: VeriSilicon operates primarily in the upstream and midstream segments of the semiconductor supply chain, focusing on semiconductor IP development and chip design services. It outsources wafer manufacturing, packaging, and testing to specialized foundries and subcontractors, maintaining a fabless business model with a wafer foundry-neutral strategy to mitigate supply chain risks.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company prioritizes R&D in AI-related IPs (NPU, GPU, GPGPU), Chiplet technology for modular chip design, and advanced packaging solutions targeting AIGC and smart mobility applications. It invests heavily in low-power IoT wireless connectivity IPs based on FD-SOI technology and automotive-grade IPs compliant with ISO 26262 safety standards. VeriSilicon also emphasizes software platform development, system-level chip customization, and ecosystem building around RISC-V architecture and open-source collaborations.
categories.revenue_model: VeriSilicon generates revenue through licensing fees for semiconductor IP cores, including upfront license fees and royalties based on chip production volumes. It also earns income from one-stop chip customization services, including chip design fees and volume production management fees. Additional revenue streams include software development services, platform solutions, and technical support contracts.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: VeriSilicon is the leading semiconductor IP supplier in China and ranks eighth globally by IP licensing revenue. It competes with global semiconductor IP providers and chip design service companies, maintaining a strong position through its comprehensive IP portfolio, advanced technology, and integrated chip design services. Its unique SiPaaS business model and early adoption of Chiplet technology differentiate it from traditional fabless chip companies and pure IP vendors.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, VeriSilicon reported revenues of approximately RMB 2.32 billion, stable compared to 2023, with a net loss attributable to shareholders of RMB 600.9 million. The company maintains total assets of RMB 4.63 billion and equity attributable to shareholders of RMB 2.12 billion. R&D investment accounted for 53.72% of revenue in 2024, reflecting a significant increase and commitment to innovation. The company has a solid order backlog and growing international sales, indicating a positive growth trajectory despite current losses.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: VeriSilicon offers a unique integrated platform combining a broad and advanced semiconductor IP portfolio with one-stop chip customization services and software solutions, enabling customers to reduce design risk, shorten time-to-market, and lower costs. Its fabless, foundry-neutral model and strong R&D capabilities in AI, Chiplet, and low-power IoT technologies provide competitive advantages. The company’s focus on safety-certified automotive IPs and ecosystem development around RISC-V and open-source projects further enhance its differentiation and appeal to diverse high-growth markets.
